To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) CDOM absorption spectra in the oxygen minimum zone (OMZ) off Peru show distinct differences from the open-ocean spectra, 2) the CDOM absorption coefficient at 355 nm, a _{CDOM} (355), is a good proxy for the CDOM absorption spectra, 3) CDOM fluorescence spectra in the OMZ are similar to the open-ocean fluorescence spectra and 4) CDOM fluorescence is not a good proxy for CDOM absorption spectra.

(1) CDOM absorption and fluorescence are highly variable in the OMZ, (2) CDOM absorption is strongly correlated with fluorescence and with the concentration of chromophoric dissolved organic matter (cDOM) in surface waters but not in subsurface waters, and (3) CDOM absorption, fluorescence, and cDOM in surface waters are correlated with the concentration of chlorophyll a and with the abundance of phytoplankton.

CDOM and FDOM in and above the OMZ off Peru are characterized by a high degree of molecular heterogeneity, which is reflected in a high diversity of CDOM fluorescence excitation-emission matrices and FDOM fluorescence spectra.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of DOM in the oxygen minimum zone (OMZ) off Peru and the adjacent oxygenated waters.
the chemical characterization of DOM in the Peru upwelling area, which is a region of high primary productivity, high export of particulate organic matter, and a deep, persistent oxygen minimum zone.
the chemical composition of the water column and how it is related to the physical and biological processes that occur in the OMZ.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

1) the DOM in the OMZ is dominated by terrestrial DOM, 2) the DOM in and above the OMZ is characterized by a higher fluorescence index, 3) the DOM in surface waters is characterized by a low fluorescence index, and 4) there is a significant correlation between fluorescence and chromophoric DOM (CDOM) absorption coefficients.
the oxygen minimum zone is a source of CDOM, but not a source of FDOM.

there are no significant differences in the chromophoric and fluorescent DOM properties in the OMZ compared to the overlying waters, but that the DOM properties are significantly different between the OMZ and the underlying waters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DOM in the OMZ off Peru is characterized by high fluorescence and chromophoricity, and is dominated by a single fluorescent component, which is likely of microbial origin.

we have found evidence that the oxygen minimum zone is a source of dissolved organic matter to the surface ocean.
